```{r}
cat_vars
#Due to tedious and repeation of same work i create a function to do all the work at once----

  analyze_categorical <- function(data) {
    results <- data.frame(Variables = character(),Catagory = character(), Frequency = integer(), Percentage = numeric(), Cumulative_freq = integer())
    
    for (var in cat_vars) {
      freq <- table(data[[var]])
      perc <- prop.table(freq) * 100
      cum_freq <- cumsum(freq)
      
      result <- data.frame(
        Variables = c(var,rep("-",length(freq)-1)),
        Category = names(freq),
        Frequency = as.vector(freq),
        Percentage = round(as.vector(perc), 2),
        Cumulative_Frequency = as.vector(cum_freq)
      )
      results <- rbind(results, result)
    }
    results
  }

analyze_categorical(data)
  

```

#Question-6
```{r informal test of normality}
#Collecting numerical variables in a dataframe
num_vars <- names(data)[sapply(data, is.numeric)]
num_vars
#function to generate Q-Q plot for all the numerical variables
qq_plot <- function(data){
  
  for (var in num_vars) {
    a<-ggplot(data, aes(sample = .data[[var]])) + 
        stat_qq(color = "blue", size = 0.9) +
        stat_qq_line(color = "cyan") +
        ggtitle(paste("Q-Q Plot of variable :",var)) +
        xlab("Theoratical Quantiles") +
        ylab("Sample Quantiles")+
        theme_light()
    print(a)      
  }
  
}

qq_plot(data)



print("Comment : From the q-q plot its quiet evident that the numerical variables Age, Height, Weight, CH2o doesn't follow normal distribution as the quantile values doesn't lie on the 45deg line.")
```

```{r formal test of normality}
#testing normality of numerical variable variables using shapiro wilk normality test
check_normality <- function(data){
  q6_result <- data.frame(Variables = character(0),Statistics = numeric(0),P_value = numeric(0))
  
  for (var in num_vars) {
    p <- shapiro.test(data[[var]])
    
    q6_result <- rbind(q6_result, data.frame(Variable = var, Statistic = p$statistic, P_Value = p$p.value))
  }
  print(q6_result)
}
check_normality(data)


print("As the P_Value of Shapiro-wilk normality test for the numerical variables Age, Height, Weight, ch2o less than 0.05. We may reject null hypothesis for 5% level of significance and conclude that the variables(Age, Height, Weight,ch2o) doesn't follow normal distribution")
```

```{r Approprieat summary Measure for non-normal data}
#function to calclate summary measures

sum_measure <- function(data) {
  stat <- data.frame(Variables = character(),Median = numeric(),First_Quartile = numeric(), Third_Quartile=numeric(), IQR = numeric(), CQD = numeric())
  
  for (var in num_vars) {
    med <- round(median(data[[var]], na.rm = T),2)
    q1  <- round(quantile(data[[var]], 0.25, na.rm = T),2)
    q3  <- round(quantile(data[[var]], 0.75, na.rm = T),2)
    iqr <- round(IQR(data[[var]], na.rm = T),2)
    cqd <- round((q3-q1/q3+q1),2)
    
    r <- data.frame(
      Variables = var,
      Median = as.vector(med),
      First_Quartile = as.vector(q1),
      Third_Quartile = as.vector(q3),
      IQR = as.vector(iqr),
      CQD = as.vector(cqd)
    )
    
    stat <- rbind(stat,r)
  }
  stat
}

sum_measure(data)

```

```{r Graphs for non-normal data}
box_plot <- function(data) {
  graphs <- list()
  
  for (var in num_vars) {
    p <- ggplot(data, aes(.data[[var]]))+
    geom_boxplot(fill = "lightblue" , color = "black", varwidth = T)+
    ggtitle(paste("Box plot of :",var))
    
    graphs[[var]] <- p
  }
  graphs
}

box_plot(data)
```

#Question-7 Pending
```{r}
# Libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
# Numerical and Categorical variables
numerical_variables <- c("Age", "Height", "Weight", "FCVC","CH2O")
categorical_variables <- c("Gender", "SMOKE","family_history_with_overweight", "FAVC", "SCC", "CALC")
# Convert categorical variables to factors
Obs <- data %>% mutate(across(all_of(categorical_variables),as.factor))
# Summary statistics
calculate_summary <- function(data, num_var, cat_var) {data %>% group_by(.data[[cat_var]]) %>%
summarise(
Min = min(.data[[num_var]], na.rm = TRUE),
Max = max(.data[[num_var]], na.rm = TRUE),
Mean = mean(.data[[num_var]], na.rm = TRUE),
Median = median(.data[[num_var]], na.rm = TRUE),
Mode = as.numeric(names(sort(table(.data[[num_var]]),
decreasing = TRUE)[1])),
Q1 = quantile(.data[[num_var]], 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
Q3 = quantile(.data[[num_var]], 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
SD = sd(.data[[num_var]], na.rm = TRUE),
Variance = var(.data[[num_var]], na.rm = TRUE),
Coef_Variation = SD / Mean,
IQR = Q3 - Q1,
Coef_Quartile_Deviation = IQR / (Q3 + Q1)
)}
# Graphs
plot_graphs <- function(data, num_var, cat_var) {
ggplot(data, aes_string(x = cat_var, y = num_var)) +
geom_boxplot(fill = "red", alpha = 0.7) +
ggtitle(paste("Boxplot of", num_var, "by", cat_var)) +
theme_minimal()}
# Subgroup analysis
for (cat_var in categorical_variables) {
  for (num_var in numerical_variables) {
    cat("\nSummary statistics for", num_var, "by", cat_var,"\n")
    print(calculate_summary(Obs, num_var, cat_var))
    print(plot_graphs(Obs, num_var, cat_var))
  }
}


```

```{r}
                     breaks = c(-Inf, 18.5, 24.9, 29.9, Inf),
```

```{r}
bmi_analysis <- function(data, x, y) {
  
  table1 <- table(data[[x]], data[[y]])
  
  #row percentage
  row_percent <- prop.table(table1,1)*100
  
  #column percentage
  col_percent <- prop.table(table1,2)*100
  
  #total percentage
  total_percent <- prop.table(table1)*100
  
  #Chi-square test
  chisq_test <- chisq.test(table1)
  expected_counts <- chisq_test$expected
  
  
  return(list(
  "Contingency Table" = table1,
  "Row Percentages" = row_percent,
  "Column Percentages" = col_percent,
  "Total Percentages" = total_percent,
  "Expected Counts" = expected_counts,
  "Chi-Square Test" = chisq_test
))
  
}

#BMI with gender
bmi_analysis(data, "Gender", "BMI_cat")

#Bmi with family_history_with_overweight
bmi_analysis(data, "family_history_with_overweight", "BMI_cat")

#Bmi with smoking
bmi_analysis(data, "SMOKE", "BMI_cat")

#Bmi with FAVC
bmi_analysis(data, "FAVC", "BMI_cat")

#Bmi wiht CAEC
bmi_analysis(data, "CAEC", "BMI_cat")

#BMI with scc
bmi_analysis(data, "SCC", "BMI_cat")

#BMI with calc
bmi_analysis(data, "CALC", "BMI_cat")

#BMI wiht MTRANS
bmi_analysis(data, "MTRANS", "BMI_cat")
```

#Question-20
```{r}
#install.packages("MASS")
require(MASS)
#install.packages("car")
require(car)
#install.packages("lmtest")
require(lmtest)

??MASS

#Model building procedure----


# Full model with all predictors
full_model <- lm(BMI ~ ., data)

# Start with an empty model
empty_model <- lm(BMI ~ 1, data)

#forward selection----
forward_model <- step(empty_model, 
                      scope = list(lower = empty_model, upper = full_model), 
                      direction = "forward")

# Summary of the final selected model
summary(forward_model)

#backward selection----
backward_model <- step(full_model,
                      direction = "backward")

# Summary of the final selected model
summary(backward_model)

#stepwise selection----
stepwise_model <- step(empty_model, 
                      scope = list(lower = empty_model, upper = full_model), 
                      direction = "both")

# Summary of the final selected model
summary(stepwise_model)

AIC(full_model)
AIC(forward_model)
AIC(backward_model)
AIC(stepwise_model)

confint(stepwise_model)

#variance in flation factor from car package
vif(stepwise_model)

```

```{r}
#normality check

        stat_qq(color = "blue", size = 0.9) +
        stat_qq_line(color = "cyan") +
        ggtitle(paste("Q-Q Plot of residual")) +
        xlab("Theoratical Quantiles") +
        ylab("Sample Quantiles")+
        theme_light()


#linearity Check
ggplot(stepwise_model, aes(x=stepwise_model$fitted.values, y=stepwise_model$residuals))+
  geom_point(colour = "red", fill = "black", shape = 23)+
  ggtitle(paste("Residual VS fitted Plot")) +
  xlab("Residuals") +
  ylab("Fitted values")+
  theme_light()


```

```{r}

# Compute Cook's distance
cooks_dist <- cooks.distance(stepwise_model)

# Plot Cook's Distance
plot(cooks_dist, main = "Cook's Distance", type = "h", col = "red")
abline(h = 4/(nrow(data)), col = "blue", lty = 8)  # Threshold line

#leverage test
hatvalues <- hatvalues(stepwise_model)
plot(hatvalues, main = "Leverage Values", type = "h", col = "blue")
abline(h = 2*mean(hatvalues), col = "red", lty = 2)



```

#Question-10

```{r}
#calculating BMI
data1$BMI <- round(data1$Weight / (data1$Height)^2,1)

# Categorize BMI
data1$BMI_cat <- cut(data1$BMI, 
                     breaks = c(-Inf, 18.5, 24.9, 29.9, Inf), 
                     labels = c("Underweight", "Normal", "Overweight", "Obesity"))

table(data1$BMI_cat)

data1$BMI_cat[data1$BMI < 18.5] <- "Underweight"
data1$BMI_cat[18.5 <= data1$BMI & data1$BMI <= 24.9] <- "Normal"
data1$BMI_cat[25 <= data1$BMI & data1$BMI <= 29.9] <- "Overweight"
data1$BMI_cat[data1$BMI >= 30] <- "Obesity"
```

```{r}
#Corr between age and bmi

r <- round(cor(data1$Age,data1$BMI),3)

#Alternative Ha : Roh(Age,BMI) != 0

corr.test(data1$Age,data1$BMI, method = "spearman")

#print(corr.test(data$Age,data$BMI),short = F)

print("Alternative Ha : Roh(Age,BMI) != 0")

print('As the p value < 0.05 we may reject null hypothesis at 5% level of significance and conclude that the correlation between Age and BMI significantly differ from Zero at 5% level of significance.')
```
